newsitem.title: USA: USDA to issue national cheddar cheese price data.
newsitem.headline: USDA to issue national cheddar cheese price data.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department will begin reporting a national cheddar cheese price on a monthly basis, it was announced Thursday.
The decision by Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman was announced by Wisconsin Senators Russ Feingold and Herb Kohl, who wanted an improved price reporting system for cheese.

In a letter, Glickman said the USDA, as a pilot program, would collect cheddar cheese price data from 200 U.S. manufacturing plants as part of its Dairy Products report. His letter did not say when the new cheddar cheese price series would become available.
"After reviewing our cheese price reporting program, I believe that it would be beneficial to report a probability- based national average cheddar cheese price," Glickman wrote.
The effort would begin as a pilot project to see if there will be enough voluntary cooperation to produce a reliable price estimate.
He also said USDA would examine data from 40 cheese plants across the country on the price and volume of sales during a 30-month period.
In a statement, Feingold said a USDA cheddar-cheese price would be "the only...reliable and consistent" data.
"Gathering cheese price informaton from other markets is an important first step in reforming the National Cheese Exchange," Kohl said.
